As others suggest, give the 30 day free trial a go and see if it's for you. It wasn't for me. Two problems. First was that it didn't like the RAW images from my Nikon D3200 camera. Exchanging email with the author (initially very responsive!) seemed to settle on a firmware update to the camera (officially downloaded from Nikon) that broke his RAW decoder. Promises to fix it, but never saw one, and I never found a way to back-rev the camera. [...] >  seemed to settle on a firmware update to the camera (officially downloaded from Nikon) that broke his RAW decoder. Promises to fix it, but never saw one, and I never found a way to back-rev the camera.
> 
> 
> Second issue was that the User Interface kind of bugged me. It hid so many options within cascading layers that I quickly became overwhelmed with stuff that probably didn't matter. Perhaps it will work for you. Some have equated APP as a "Pixinsight Lite", in terms of opportunity / need to understand the details of astro image processing. Probably a good entry-level path into the nitty details of image processing, based on the limited experience I had.
> 
> [...] Quote



   #3

 Posted January 24, 2024

I'm a great fan of APP. First, I don't really like post-processing or learning new software. APP is very user friendly and won't require much learning (quite unlike PI, I've been told). I've gotten very decent results using essentially one click approaches (just load the lights and calibration frames and click 'integrate'). APP is developed and new functions are added, but not very quickly. As far as I'm concerned, this isn't a problem and I like what it delivers so consider this an endorsement of APP from someone who started out with DSS and had a stab at Siril. The trial is a very good way to find out if you like it enough.

       dpoulson   July 10, 2025 Reply [...] Breakout board

For powering the lights, you can test using a usb cable from the computer to the ESP32, but do not power this way when inside the dome, the current consumption can get too high and cause a brown out, plus the connector can be fragile and easily broken off. I recommend a decent 5v buck converter or similar (with at least 1A of current) and to power it via the screw terminals. Voltage must be 5v, lower (like 4.5 from 3\AA) will quickly drop and they’ll stop working, and may damage the ESP32 from drawing too much current. More than 5v will damage the LEDs.
